summary: The prepared_gaia variant is a design plus code submission with a GAIA PDF and a SPADE-based Python implementation split into container, communicator, and collector agents. It implements fill monitoring and basic notification to a communicator, but the collector selection is random rather than nearest, deadline handling only logs a warning, and truck-load prioritization is absent. The code also contains hardcoded SPADE credentials, which is a critical security finding under the judge rubric.

findings.description: The container agent monitors fill level and notifies the communicator when the configured full threshold is reached.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/garbage_collection_system/container_agent.py:44-58 increments current_fill, checks current_fill >= full_threshold, and sends a message to communicator@localhost.

findings.description: The nearest-truck requirement is not implemented; the communicator randomly selects a collector.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/garbage_collection_system/communicator_agent.py:91-98 says it will pick a random available collector and calls random.choice(available_collectors).

findings.description: The one-day collection requirement is not enforced; the system only logs a warning after one day.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/garbage_collection_system/container_agent.py:86-90 checks time_since_full > timedelta(days=1), logs a warning, and comments that this could trigger an emergency response.

findings.description: The requirement to prioritize more-filled garbage trucks is not represented in the collector selection logic.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/garbage_collection_system/communicator_agent.py:91-98 chooses randomly from collector_positions; CollectorAgent.current_load exists at collector_agent.py:18 but is not used in selection.

findings.description: The communicator availability filter references a status field that does not exist on CommunicatorAgent, so collector selection can fail at runtime once collector positions exist.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/garbage_collection_system/communicator_agent.py:93-94 filters with if self.agent.status != "busy", but CommunicatorAgent.__init__ at lines 13-17 defines collector_positions, container_positions, and log_file only.

findings.description: The GAIA design defines dispatcher protocols for requesting collector positions and dispatching collectors, but the implementation uses fixed collector JIDs rather than discovery or a robust coordination protocol.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/Seroidtest.pdf page 2 describes Dispatcher protocols RequestCollectorPosition and DispatchGarbageCollector; communicator_agent.py:42-44 says broadcast would be used in a real system and hardcodes collector1@localhost, collector2@localhost, and collector3@localhost.

findings.description: SPADE agent passwords are hardcoded in source.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/garbage_collection_system/main.py:15-25 creates collector, communicator, and container agents with literal passwords such as "password1", "password2", "password3", and "password".

findings.description: A behavior contains a no-op placeholder in a production path.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/garbage_collection_system/container_agent.py:60-68 defines SendContainerFullBehaviour and ends the message handling path with pass.

findings.description: Dependencies are range-based rather than pinned, reducing reproducibility.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/requirements.txt uses unpinned lower bounds for spade, asyncio, python-dateutil, and pytest.

missing_requirements: Actual nearest non-full garbage truck selection based on distance or location.
Operational enforcement that a full container is not left full for more than one day.
Prioritization of more-filled garbage trucks during assignment.
Reliable monitoring and use of truck full/free/busy state in the dispatch decision.
logical_inconsistencies: The GAIA PDF says the dispatcher chooses the nearest free garbage truck, but communicator_agent.py randomly chooses from available_collectors.
CommunicatorAgent filters collectors using self.agent.status even though CommunicatorAgent has no status attribute.
CollectorAgent.current_load is updated downward after emptying a container, which conflicts with the notion that collecting waste should increase truck load until unloading.
The one-day rule is described as a collection requirement, but the implementation only logs a warning.
implementation_risks: Collector selection can crash or behave incorrectly because CommunicatorAgent.status is undefined.
Dispatch choices can be geographically wrong because distance is not calculated.
Full containers can remain overdue because the one-day condition does not trigger a concrete action.
Hardcoded credentials make deployment unsafe and environment-specific.
Truck-load prioritization cannot work because dispatch ignores current_load.
